Put the rows in order

Source: R/table_plan.R
plan_sort.Rd

plan_sort() says the order of the rows: by the values of columns, or by frequency. On a plan with an ARD half it sorts before the cells are filled, while the statistics are still there to sort on (-n, the most frequent first); on a plan of a finished table or a listing it sorts the table. It is one verb whichever of the two does the work.

Usage

plan_sort(.plan, ..., stat = NULL, keep = TRUE)

Arguments

.plan

A table_plan().

...

The sort keys in priority order, each a string; a leading - sorts descending, ties go to the keys that follow. They are widen_ard()'s sort, where each form is described in full:

a column

a row key or the label column by its output name ("label"); on a finished table or a listing, any column ("USUBJID").

a statistic

"-n": that statistic totalled across the columns, the most frequent first.

"<stat>[<col>]"

the statistic in one column: "-n[Active]", "-n[Total]".

"<stat>@<key>"

the statistic of the group's own row, carried to every row of the group: "-n@soc" orders the SOCs by their own count and keeps each SOC's PTs with it.

"max(<stat>)", "min(<stat>)"

the largest (smallest) value across the columns instead of the total: "-max(n)".

"levels(<key>)"

the values plan_levels() names for that key first, in its order.

".overall", ".depth"

the overall rows first; a level's own row before the rows nested under it.

One logical is widen_ard(sort = ) as it is: TRUE brings a key's separate blocks together, FALSE moves only what an order declares.

stat

The statistic totalled into .sort_stat for a frequency order (widen_ard(sort_stat = )), e.g. stat = "n".

keep

FALSE also hides the sort keys that are columns: a sort carrier needed and not wanted. Names that are not columns (a statistic, ".depth") are ignored rather than refused.

Value

The plan, with one more layer.

See also

plan_verbs for every verb.

Other plan verbs: plan_after(), plan_append(), plan_blanks(), plan_cell_style(), plan_cells(), plan_col_header(), plan_columns(), plan_compare(), plan_digits(), plan_empty(), plan_filter(), plan_footnotes(), plan_hide(), plan_labels(), plan_levels(), plan_listing(), plan_nest(), plan_paginate_cols(), plan_paginate_group(), plan_paginate_rows(), plan_row_group(), plan_stat_groups(), plan_stub(), plan_style(), plan_titles(), plan_total()

Examples

ae <- data.frame(
  ARM       = rep(c("Placebo", "Active"), each = 4),
  variable  = "AEDECOD",
  .label    = rep(c("Headache", "Nausea", "Dizziness", "Rash"), 2),
  .kind     = "categorical",
  stat_name = "n",
  stat      = c(3, 1, 0, 2, 6, 4, 1, 0))
p <- table_plan(ae, cols = "ARM", rows = c(group = "variable")) |>
  plan_cells(categorical = "{n}")

# Minimal: the most frequent term first, over both arms
p |> plan_sort("-n") |> plan_apply("table")
#>     group     label Placebo Active
#> 1 AEDECOD  Headache       3      6
#> 2 AEDECOD    Nausea       1      4
#> 3 AEDECOD      Rash       2      0
#> 4 AEDECOD Dizziness       0      1

# Ordered by the active arm's count, ties alphabetical
p |> plan_sort("-n[Active]", "label") |> plan_apply("table")
#>     group     label Placebo Active
#> 1 AEDECOD  Headache       3      6
#> 2 AEDECOD    Nausea       1      4
#> 3 AEDECOD Dizziness       0      1
#> 4 AEDECOD      Rash       2      0

# On a listing it sorts the records
recs <- data.frame(USUBJID = c("01-002", "01-001", "01-001"),
                   AETERM  = c("Fatigue", "Nausea", "Headache"))
pages <- table_plan(recs) |>
  plan_sort("USUBJID", "AETERM") |>
  plan_listing(listing_col("USUBJID", label = "Subject"),
               listing_col("AETERM", label = "Adverse event")) |>
  plan_apply()
pages[[1]]
#> ─────────────────────────
#> Subject     Adverse event
#> ─────────────────────────
#> 01-001      Headache     
#>                          
#> 01-001      Nausea       
#>                          
#> 01-002      Fatigue      
#>                          
#> 
#> <rtftable> 6 rows x 3 columns
#>   Columns:    Subject |  | Adverse event
#>   Row title:  col 1
#>   Borders:    set
#>   Widths:     relative 7:1:13
#>
